# Codemap - issue 0147, unit-test-track round: the repeat cell `repeat|selectionCount|parent|child=any|repeats=1|s=true|ics=false|icf=false|roundUp=false|pct=false`

This round has no red scenario. The construct (`Grappling Hooks`, `6eac-4ed9-4511-ff14`, in the definitive `.gst`) is unreachable from any roster, so the deliverable is a synthetic unit test under `src/evaluator/` plus the coverage bookkeeping that records the cell as covered. Nothing under `docs/testing/<slug>/` is touched - every scenario's `.ros`, `scenario.json` and `README.md` is specification - and `docs/testing/campaign-state.json` belongs to the campaign driver.

## Files the issue has to change

- **`src/evaluator/<new>.test.js`** (new) - the synthetic unit test that pins the repeat's semantics. Exact name is the researcher's; the suite's convention (`src/evaluator/CLAUDE.md`, "Naming") is `<module>.<topic>.test.js` for a layer test through a module's public surface, and this file's path is the `evidence` string the coverage record has to name, so the two must agree.
- **`docs/testing/covered-cells.json`** - takes the new entry for the cell: `key`, `evidence` naming the new test file, `rationale` saying why a module test rather than a scenario carries it. The file's `_comment` already admits a module test as evidence; this is the first entry that uses it.
- **`docs/testing/worklist.json`** - regenerated by `node scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js`. Today it holds exactly this one cell with `totals {cells:105, covered:104, uncovered:1}`; afterwards it must be the empty worklist. Commit it in the same commit as `covered-cells.json`, or the drift guard sees drift.
- **`scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js`** - the drift guard hard-codes the totals: line 117, `expect(recomputed.totals).toEqual({ cells: 105, covered: 104, uncovered: 1 })`. That expectation is arithmetically false once the cell is covered, so the guard cannot pass unless this number moves. This file sits outside the issue's "Out of scope" allow-list; the acceptance criterion that the guard passes wins over that list, and the change here is confined to the totals the round actually moves - no other case in the file, and nothing about how the inventory classifies cells.

## Files that change only if the engine's reading differs from the test

The issue makes the test the specification and orders the engine fixed if it disagrees. Whether any of these is touched is unknown until the test runs; all three are already implicated in the semantics the criteria list, and none is known to be wrong today.

- **`src/evaluator/modifiers.js`** - owns the repeat itself: `repeatCount` (line ~224) turns the counted value into steps and multiplies by `repeats`, `repeatsFactor` (line ~256) sums a `<repeats>` list into the application count, and the factor reaches the modifier application at line ~644. The "one application per `value` counted selections" reading lives here.
- **`src/evaluator/query.js`** - resolves the repeat's count query against a scope and a `childId`. The `scope="parent"` counting frame and the own-share rule for the `childId="any"` / `null` target (lines ~447-451) are here; so is the `includeChildSelections="false"` restriction to a frame's direct children.
- **`src/evaluator/countIndex.js`** - builds the per-frame tallies the query reads, taking `selectionCount` from each node's `instance.count` (lines ~102-108), which is where `field="selections"` counting quantities rather than XML elements is decided.

## Read-only context the round leans on, changed by nobody

- `docs/testing/at-least-parent-any-reveal/` - README rules ALP-R5 and ALP-R2 and roster `04-wolf-lord-selected-self-reveal.ros` already pin, from real catalogue data, that the carrier counts in its own frame and that `includeChildSelections="false"` counts only the frame's direct children for the same scope/childId pair. The issue orders those readings carried over unchanged to the repeat axis.
- `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/Warhammer Fantasy Battles (6th definitive edition).gst` - holds the unreachable construct; read for its shape, never edited.
- `src/evaluator/CLAUDE.md` and `scripts/lib/CLAUDE.md` - the two suite docs that bind the new test's conventions and the drift guard's case-to-file mapping.
- Existing synthetic-dataset patterns in this suite: `countIndex.syntheticAnchors.test.js`, `offer.hiddenGate.test.js`, `countIndex.costSumCarrierFrame.test.js` (per-file catalogue factories), and `modifiers.setWithRepeat.test.js` for a repeat pinned as specification.

increments.title: Pin the parent/any repeat on a synthetic dataset and record the cell as covered
increments.goal: Close the coverage campaign's last open cell, `repeat|selectionCount|parent|child=any|repeats=1|s=true|ics=false|icf=false|roundUp=false|pct=false`, on the unit-test track: a new synthetic-dataset unit test under `src/evaluator/` that pins the repetition semantics the construct demands, the engine corrected where it reads them differently, and the coverage bookkeeping that records the cell as covered so the inventory exits 0 and the drift guard passes. This is the whole issue and it is not split: the test file's path is the evidence string the coverage record carries, and the regenerated worklist is only true once the test exists, so a first half that stops before the record leaves the campaign cell open and the bookkeeping inconsistent.
criteria: A new unit test under `src/evaluator/`, built on a synthetic dataset rather than a roster against the frozen corpus, exercises the cell `repeat|selectionCount|parent|child=any|repeats=1|s=true|ics=false|icf=false|roundUp=false|pct=false`.

The test pins each of these readings separately, so that one wrong reading cannot pass it: (a) the modifier is applied once per `value` counted selections, with frame counts of 0, 1 and 2 moving the modified value by 0, 1 and 2 applications, crossing at least two repetitions; (b) the counting frame of `scope="parent"` is the selection that holds the carrier, not the carrier itself and not a group; (c) `childId="any"` counts any selection in that frame, whatever entry it came from; (d) the carrier counts in its own frame, and with `includeChildSelections="false"` only the frame's direct children count - both carried over unchanged from rules ALP-R5 and ALP-R2 of `docs/testing/at-least-parent-any-reveal`; (e) `field="selections"` counts selection quantities, so a single child node with `number="2"` counts 2.

Where the engine evaluates the construct differently from those readings, the engine is corrected - the test is the specification here, as a scenario is in the earlier rounds - and no already-green scenario or test regresses.

`docs/testing/covered-cells.json` carries a new entry for that cell whose `evidence` names the new test file and whose `rationale` says why the cell is covered by a module test rather than by a scenario.
`node scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js` exits 0, and the worklist it regenerates is committed in the same commit as the coverage record.

`npx vitest run scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js` passes - which requires its hard-coded totals expectation (`{ cells: 105, covered: 104, uncovered: 1 }`, line 117) to move to the totals the covered cell produces. That is the only change permitted in that file.
`npx vitest run src/evaluator` ends with no failing case.
Nothing under `docs/testing/<slug>/` and nothing in `docs/testing/campaign-state.json` is changed.

Reading the engine end to end (modifiers.js repeatCount/repeatsFactor, query.js resolveFrame/includeFrameOwn, countIndex.js FRAME_OWN and the crossing buckets) it already implements all five readings the criteria demand, so no engine change is planned - the test is written as the specification and only a failing case would justify touching the engine.

## What this increment builds

Three things, in one commit: a new synthetic-dataset unit test under `src/evaluator/` that pins the repeat construct of `Grappling Hooks`; the coverage record that credits the cell to that test file; and the regenerated worklist plus the drift guard's moved totals. The test file's path is the `evidence` string of the coverage record, so the two must name the same path - `src/evaluator/modifiers.repeatParentAny.test.js`.

The test file itself and the one-line totals edit in `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js` are specified in `testPlan` and belong to the test-author. What follows is the implementer's half.

## The engine: expected to need no change

I read every line the construct passes through and found no disagreement with the five readings the criteria demand. Do not pre-emptively change anything here. Make the new test pass; only a case that actually fails justifies an engine edit, and then the test is the specification, not the engine.

The reading, so a failure can be located instead of guessed:

- **One application per `value` counted selections** - `repeatCount` (`src/evaluator/modifiers.js:224-233`) computes `steps = floor(actual / perValue)` (`ceil` under `roundUp`) and returns `steps * repeat.repeats`. With `value="1"` and `repeats="1"` the mapping frame-count -> applications is the identity. `repeatsFactor` (`:256-263`) sums a `<repeats>` list; a single repeat passes its count through. `applyModifier` (`:644`) multiplies that into `times`, and the arithmetic is `addValue = (current, operand, times) => current + operand * times` (`:499`). So an `increment 1` on a cost type raises the carrier's effective per-instance cost by exactly the counted number.
- **The counting frame of `scope="parent"`** - `resolveFrame` (`src/evaluator/query.js:205-218`) returns `ctx.node.parent` for `PARENT` **before** it looks at `shared`, so `shared="true"` does not widen it. `ctx.node` is the node whose modifiers are running (`modifiers.js:754-760`, `applyModifiersOfNodes` builds the query context with `node`), i.e. the carrier occurrence, so the frame is the selection that holds the carrier. A `selectionEntryGroup` never becomes that frame: group members are direct children of the owner selection in the eval tree, and the group anchor is a phantom **sibling** attached under the owner (`evalTree.js:880-911`, `attachGroupAnchor` / `annotateGroupMembers`). Offer anchors also attach to the real owner frame, not to a group anchor (`offer.js:196, 222-238`, `optionDefinitionsUnder` flattens through groups).
- **`childId="any"` counts any selection in the frame** - the reader maps `childId="any"` to the `null` target (`catalogReader.js:562`), and `targetsOf` (`countIndex.js:150-161`) lists `null` for every non-force selection whatever entry it came from.
- **The carrier counts in its own frame; `includeChildSelections="false"` counts only direct children** - `indexNodeContribution` (`countIndex.js:231-313`) walks each node's ancestor chain; in the node's **own** frame the `null`-target share goes into the separate `FRAME_OWN` slot, in every ancestor frame it goes into the crossing bucket chosen by how many boundaries were crossed. A direct child of the frame lands in `BASE`, a grandchild in `SELECTION`. `query.js:456-462` passes `includeFrameOwn = frame === ctx.node`, which is `false` for a `parent` frame, so the frame does not count itself, while the carrier - a direct child of that frame - does. `combineBuckets` (`countIndex.js:331-348`) adds `SELECTION` only under `includeChildSelections`, so `false` excludes a grandchild. These are exactly rules ALP-R5 and ALP-R2 of `docs/testing/at-least-parent-any-reveal/README.md`, and ALP-R4 there states the same frame rule ("der Eltern-Rahmen ist die umschliessende Auswahl, nicht die Gruppe").
- **`field="selections"` counts quantities** - `contributionOf` (`countIndex.js:101-109`) takes `selectionCount` from `node.instance.count`, which is the `.ros` `number` attribute (`src/evaluator/__fixtures__/rosParser.js:56` maps `number` to `count`). One selection node with `number="2"` contributes 2.

If a case does fail, the three files above are the only plausible sites; correct the one that misreads, and re-run the whole evaluator suite so no green scenario regresses.

## The coverage record

Append one entry to the `cells` array of `docs/testing/covered-cells.json` (array order is not significant; append at the end). Only `key` is read mechanically - `keysFromCoveredRecord` (`scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-cells.js:676-679`) takes the key and ignores the rest - so `evidence` and `rationale` are for human readers and must carry the reasoning. Use this entry verbatim:

```json
{
  "key": "repeat|selectionCount|parent|child=any|repeats=1|s=true|ics=false|icf=false|roundUp=false|pct=false",
  "evidence": [
    "src/evaluator/modifiers.repeatParentAny.test.js"
  ],
  "rationale": "Covered by a module test rather than by a scenario, because the corpus's only occurrence is unreachable from any roster: the carrier 'Grappling Hooks' (6eac-4ed9-4511-ff14, a shared selectionEntry of src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/Warhammer Fantasy Battles (6th definitive edition).gst) is named exactly once in the whole corpus - at its own definition - nothing links it, it carries no categoryLink, and the game system declares no forceEntries, so no .ros can put it into a parent frame. The maintainer decided on 2026-08-11 (docs/testing/campaign-state.json, parkedQuestions) to cover the cell on the unit-test track instead of waiving it as untestable, because the entry models a real rule of the game - 1 point per grappling hook and rope, one per model of a skirmishing infantry unit, matching the entry's own comment '1p/model' - and the missing incoming link is an upstream data gap, not a meaningless construct. The test rebuilds the construct on a synthetic catalogue (increment +1 on a cost type, one repeat with field=selections scope=parent childId=any value=1 repeats=1 shared=true includeChildSelections=false includeChildForces=false roundUp=false percentValue=false) and pins five readings separately, so no single wrong reading can pass it: one application per counted selection across frame counts 0, 1, 2 and 3; the counting frame being the selection that holds the carrier, neither the carrier itself nor the enclosing selectionEntryGroup; childId=any counting a selection of a foreign entry; the carrier counting in its own frame while a grandchild is excluded by includeChildSelections=false (rules ALP-R5 and ALP-R2 of docs/testing/at-least-parent-any-reveal carried over unchanged to the repeat axis); and field=selections counting quantities, so one selection with number=2 counts 2."
}
```

## The regenerated worklist

Run `node scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js` from the repository root **after** the record above is in place. It rewrites `docs/testing/worklist.json` itself (`scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js:95`) and must then exit 0 - `exitCodeFor` returns 0 exactly when the worklist is empty. The regenerated file must show `"totals": { "cells": 105, "covered": 105, "uncovered": 0 }` and an empty `"cells": []`. Commit it in the same commit as `covered-cells.json`; the drift guard recomputes the worklist and deep-equals it against the committed file, so a stale committed file is drift.

## Order of work

1. The test file exists (test-author).
2. Engine: run the evaluator suite; correct only what fails.
3. `docs/testing/covered-cells.json` gets the entry above.
4. `node scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js` regenerates `docs/testing/worklist.json`; exit 0.
5. The drift guard's totals line is already moved by the test-author; re-run it.

## Boundaries this increment keeps

Nothing under `docs/testing/<slug>/` is touched - every scenario's `.ros`, `scenario.json` and `README.md` is specification. `docs/testing/campaign-state.json` belongs to the campaign driver and is not edited. In `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js` only the numeric literal on line 117 changes; no other case, no comment, nothing about how the inventory classifies cells.

## Alternatives considered and rejected

- **Waiving the cell instead of covering it.** Rejected by the maintainer on 2026-08-11 and recorded in `campaign-state.json`; the issue restates it as a decision. Not reopened here.
- **A `.ros` fixture against the frozen corpus.** Impossible: the carrier has no incoming link and the `.gst` declares no `forceEntries`, so no admissible roster reaches it. That is why the criteria demand a synthetic dataset.
- **Observing the construct through a modified constraint bound instead of a cost.** The corpus occurrence increments a cost type (`ecfa-8486-4f6c-c249`), and `capability.costs[costTypeId]` reports the effective per-instance cost after modifiers, at occupied slots and at offer anchors alike (`report.js:400-404, 437`; `costProjection.js:62-90`). Mirroring the real construct keeps the test honest about what the cell is; a constraint bound would pin a different modifier target.
- **Getting a frame count of 0 with the carrier selected.** Impossible by construction once ALP-R5 holds: a selected carrier is itself a direct child of its parent frame and contributes at least its own quantity. The only frame count of 0 is at the carrier's **offer anchor** in an empty frame, which is where the test pins the zero-application reading. This is a finding, not a workaround, and belongs in the test file's header comment.
- **Building the test at the tree/index layer (`buildIndex` + `query`) instead of through `prepareDataset`/`evaluate`.** Rejected: the rule spans the reader, the query, the index and the modifier arithmetic, and the suite doc's rule is to observe at the narrowest layer that can see the rule - here that is the facade, because the observable is the reported effective cost.

return.testPlan:
## Whether

Tests are needed, and the test **is** the deliverable of this increment: a new synthetic-dataset unit test under `src/evaluator/`, plus a one-line edit in the existing drift guard.

## What is already red

I ran nothing - not the suite, not the inventory, not the guard. State of the tree as read: the new test file does not exist; `docs/testing/worklist.json` holds the one open cell with `totals { cells: 105, covered: 104, uncovered: 1 }`; `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js:117` asserts exactly those totals and therefore passes today. Once you move that literal to `{ cells: 105, covered: 105, uncovered: 0 }` the guard goes red and stays red until the implementer adds the coverage record and regenerates the worklist. That is the intended red, not a mistake.

## File 1 (new): `src/evaluator/modifiers.repeatParentAny.test.js`

Name by the suite's `<module>.<topic>.test.js` convention: the rule is the repeat's arithmetic, and `modifiers.js` owns it (the sibling repeat test is `modifiers.setWithRepeat.test.js`). **This exact path is the `evidence` string of the coverage record - do not rename it.**

Level: layer test through the public facade `prepareDataset` + `evaluate` from `./evaluator.js`, observed on `report.capabilities`. Framework: vitest. Run it alone with `npx vitest run src/evaluator/modifiers.repeatParentAny.test.js`.

Header comment to carry (in English, as the suite doc asks for new comments): the cell key, the unreachable corpus occurrence `Grappling Hooks` `6eac-4ed9-4511-ff14`, why a synthetic dataset rather than a `.ros`, and the finding that a frame count of 0 is only observable at the carrier's offer anchor because a selected carrier always counts itself (ALP-R5).

### The synthetic catalogue

One per-file factory (or one module-level constant, since every case shares the skeleton) built as an inline XML string. Shape, with the ids named as constants:

- `<forceEntry id="force-army" name="Army"/>`.
- `selectionEntry` `entry-unit` (`type="unit"`), holding:
  - a `<selectionEntryGroups>` with one `selectionEntryGroup` `group-gear` carrying a `max` constraint (`value="5" field="selections" scope="parent" shared="true" includeChildSelections="false" includeChildForces="false"`, so a group anchor is actually synthesised and never fires), and inside it the **carrier**;
  - a `<selectionEntries>` with two plain sibling upgrades of different entries, `entry-shield` and `entry-torch`, both outside the group and without costs.
- The carrier `entry-hooks` (`type="upgrade"`), with `<costs><cost name="Points" typeId="cost-points" value="5"/></costs>` - a non-zero base cost, so "zero applications" is visibly different from "no cost at all" - and the modifier, written exactly as the corpus writes it:

```xml
<modifiers>
  <modifier type="increment" field="cost-points" value="1">
    <repeats>
      <repeat field="selections" scope="parent" value="1" percentValue="false"
              shared="true" includeChildSelections="false" includeChildForces="false"
              childId="any" repeats="1" roundUp="false"/>
    </repeats>
  </modifier>
</modifiers>
```

- Under the carrier, one nested child `entry-rope` (`type="upgrade"`, its own `cost-points` value `0`) - the grandchild that `includeChildSelections="false"` must exclude.

No `<costTypes>` declaration is needed: the modifier target resolves because `cost-points` appears in a definition's `<costs>`, and `capability.costs` is filled regardless of `declaredCostTypeIds`.

Rosters are the plain object shape `{ forces: [{ defId, count, children }] }` that `evaluate` takes; group membership never appears in a roster, so the carrier is always a direct child of the unit node.

Helpers: one `evaluate(rosterObject)` wrapper over `evaluateDataset(prepareDataset({ catalogues: [XML] }), roster)`, and one capability lookup that takes a `defId` **and an expected `anchorKind`** (`AnchorKind.OCCUPIED` / `AnchorKind.OFFER_ANCHOR` from `./model.js`) and asserts the record was found - so an occupied slot can never silently answer for an anchor or the other way round. The pattern for both is `countIndex.frameOwnAnyTarget.test.js`.

### The cases

Every case asserts `capability.costs['cost-points']` of the carrier. Base cost is 5, so the expected value is `5 + <counted selections>`. Give each `it()` a German title, one rule each, per the suite doc.

| # | Criterion | Roster (children of the selected unit) | Observed slot | Expected `costs['cost-points']` | What a wrong reading would give |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | (a) zero applications | none - the unit is selected and empty | carrier's OFFER anchor | **5** | 6 if the modifier fired unconditionally once |
| 2 | (a)+(d) the carrier counts itself | `[hooks]` | carrier OCCUPIED | **6** | 5 if the carrier were excluded from its own frame |
| 3 | (a)+(c) second repetition, foreign entry | `[hooks, shield]` | carrier OCCUPIED | **7** | 6 if only one application ever fired; 6 if a foreign entry did not count under `childId="any"` |
| 4 | (c) any entry, third repetition | `[hooks, shield, torch]` | carrier OCCUPIED | **8** | 7 if the second foreign entry did not count |
| 5 | (e) quantities, not elements | `[hooks, shield {count: 2}]` | carrier OCCUPIED | **8** | 7 if XML selection elements were counted instead of quantities |
| 6 | (b)+(d) frame is the holder; grandchild excluded | `[hooks -> [rope {count: 3}], shield]` | carrier OCCUPIED | **7** | 10 with `includeChildSelections="true"` semantics (1+3+1); 9 if the frame were the carrier itself with its own share (1+3); 8 if the frame were the carrier without its own share (3); 5 if the frame were the `group-gear` anchor |
| 7 | (c) `childId="any"` at an anchor | `[shield]` only, carrier unselected | carrier's OFFER anchor | **6** | 5 if a foreign entry did not count under the `null` target |

Case 6 is the discriminator that separates four readings at once - keep its `rope` quantity at 3 so no two readings collide on the same number, and say so in a code comment.

Cases 1 and 2 together cross the boundary from zero to one application; cases 2, 3 and 4 cross the second and third repetition, so "crossing at least two repetitions" is met with room to spare.
